# The 29 cases the two annotators labell: # Released so the classification can be re-derived or contested (paper Sec. 4.5).

column6: arbiter_note
The annotators agree the faulty statement is reached and differ on which later condition fails; the arbiter follows the stack trace of the developer's triggering test.
One annotator read the fixture setup as the obstacle, the other the oracle; the triggering test fails on an assertion, not on construction, so the oracle reading stands.
Disagreement turns on whether the collaborator is external: it is stubbed in the project's own test harness, which places the bug in reachability rather than environment.
Both labels are defensible for a fault that needs two calls in order; the arbiter takes the sequence as the binding obstacle, since the second call alone reproduces nothing.
The annotators differ on whether a thrown exception counts as an available oracle; here the exception is swallowed by a catch block, so no oracle is available.
One reading blames object construction, the other the absence of an assertion; the generated suite does construct the object, which settles it against construction.
The fault surfaces only under a non-default locale, which one annotator classified as state and the other as environment; the arbiter follows the latter.
A borderline case where the faulty branch is reached but the state is not infected; recorded under infection, with the disagreement noted rather than resolved on the merits.
The annotators split on a helper that reads the clock; since the helper is called transitively rather than directly, the arbiter keeps the environment label.
Disagreement over whether a deeply nested builder counts as complex construction; the arbiter counts constructor arity rather than nesting depth, which places it here.
One annotator treated a checked exception as the revealing signal; the triggering test asserts on a returned value instead, so revealability is not the obstacle.
The bug needs a resource that the harness provides; whether that makes it environmental depends on the harness, and the arbiter treats the harness as part of the project.
